sections.heading: Brands Scan Better With a Face
paragraphs: A plain QR code communicates, but a code with your logo communicates who you are. QR codes with logos turn packaging, posters and cards into branded experiences that also drive traffic.
The logo anchors trust: recipients know exactly what they are scanning.
ChooseTools creates branded QR codes locally in your browser, embedding your image into the code pattern with scannability preserved.
Marketing teams report higher scan rates when a recognizable logo sits in the code center, because the visual cue reduces hesitation about unknown destinations.

sections.heading: How to Create a QR Code With Your Logo
paragraphs: Branded and scannable in a few clicks.
Paste your target URL. Upload a logo, ideally square PNG, and position it in the center. Choose error correction high enough for safe scanning, then export.
Rendering is local, so your logo and payload stay on your machine.
The exported file downloads directly to your device, ready for print layouts, digital campaigns or social media posts.

sections.heading: Error Correction: The Key to Logo-Centric Scans
paragraphs: A logo in the code center physically covers modules; higher error correction levels rebuild the missing data when scanning.
The generator defaults to robust correction when a logo is present.
This balance keeps the design and the scannability both intact.
Error correction level H allows up to thirty percent of modules to be obscured, which gives ample room for a logo while still decoding reliably on modern phones.

sections.heading: Business Cards, Packaging and Posters
paragraphs: Embedding the mark in the card's code signals provenance before a single scan completes.
Packaging, banners, windows and menus all carry branded codes that drive home the brand.
Consistent branded codes across surfaces build recognition.
Trade show exhibitors place branded QR codes on booth graphics so attendees can capture contact details instantly without typing a URL.

sections.heading: Logo Sizing and Quiet Zone Rules
paragraphs: The logo should be large enough to be recognizable but small enough to leave the surrounding quiet zone untouched, because scanners depend on that margin to detect the code boundary.
A safe rule is to keep the logo within twenty percent of the code area, though higher error correction relaxes this constraint.
Testing the exported code on several phone models before printing catches edge-case scan failures early.

sections.heading: Scanning Distance and Print Size
paragraphs: The physical size of the printed code determines the minimum scanning distance; larger codes scan from farther away and are more reliable in low-light environments.
A code that is too small on a business card may fail to decode on older phone cameras, even if the digital resolution is high.
Balancing logo size, error correction and print dimensions ensures the final product scans reliably under real-world conditions.

sections.heading: Design Control: Colors, Corners, Quiet Zones
paragraphs: Style code modules and a clean quiet zone to match the brand palette without breaking scan reliability.
Keep contrast high enough for phone cameras in all lighting.
Beauty follows function.
Dark modules on a light background remain the most universally scannable combination, even though colored codes look striking in digital mock-ups.

sections.heading: Private Branded QR Creation
paragraphs: Your logo is your identity; generating with it locally means no third party ever sees placement.
No upload, no account, no watermark — across all platforms.
Brand and payload, both yours.
Pre-release campaign assets and confidential event invitations stay private when logo embedding and code generation happen entirely within the browser.

sections.heading: Replacing and Refreshing Campaigns
paragraphs: When a campaign URL changes or a seasonal offer expires, the corresponding QR code must be regenerated with the new destination.
Recreating a branded code locally allows rapid iteration and immediate distribution, without waiting on an external service to update.
Keeping the same logo and design while altering only the payload means the visual identity stays consistent even as promotions rotate.

faqs.q: Will a logo in the center break scanning?
faqs.a: Not if error correction is high enough and contrast remains strong; the generator sets robustness appropriately for logo-bearing codes.

faqs.q: What logo format should I upload?
faqs.a: A square PNG logo with transparent or matching background works best; position, size and quiet-zone controls fine-tune the result.
Yes. Both the payload and your logo are processed locally in your browser with no uploads or accounts.

faqs.q: What error correction level should I choose?
faqs.a: Level H or Q is recommended when embedding a logo, because they tolerate significant module coverage while maintaining reliable scanning.
